title: Seasonal Flavors and the Variety Pack
lessons: The player notices Liquid I.V. because a seasonal flavor is built around a familiar candy or frozen-treat brand.
The player already uses Liquid I.V. and buys a variety pack instead of committing to one flavor.

text: Cooler, sand, someone's phone speaker. A Liquid I.V. packet in the bag has a candy brand's logo on it. Firecracker. You know that one from a freezer aisle when you were nine.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You made hydration taste like a childhood freezer aisle.

entry-first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: When you say it like that, yes. I'm not going to defend it. I wanted to see if it worked, and it worked on you.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: The familiar name is doing a lot of the work you should be doing.

entry-first-4.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: That's the whole reason to do a collaboration. People picked Firecracker off the shelf because they knew the name before they read one electrolyte number. I'd like it to be me, but it was the popsicle.

choice-first.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You're holding it and squinting at it. Are we doing this?

choices.text: That sounds fun enough to throw in the cooler.
Nostalgia has nothing to do with staying hydrated.
I don't want candy logic in the bag I actually rely on.

first-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then the memory got you to taste it. What's inside is the same as always, and it's going to be doing more than the popsicle did today.

first-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I resent how effective that is.

first-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Nope. Nothing. Hold me to that. The flavor gets you to look. The stuff inside still has to earn the bag, same as any other packet.

first-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Then skip it and grab the flavor you already trust. It's in the same bag. I'm not going to talk you into the fun one.
You bought the variety pack again. You're already digging past two flavors to get to the same two you always drink.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: I keep buying the variety pack and grabbing the same two packets first.

entry-return-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: That still counts as variety. Technically. The other two are in there for the day you wake up bored.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why not just sell me those two and stop tempting me with the rest?

entry-return-4.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: You can buy just those two. I'll say that once. The pack exists for the week the routine starts feeling like a chore and a new flavor is the cheapest way out of that.

choice-return.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: What's it going to be, the usual or one of the ones you keep skipping?

choices.text: I like being able to choose based on my mood.
This feels like a fix for me getting bored of you.
If I need four flavors to stay interested, maybe I don't need the habit.

return-1.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Good. Then the other two aren't dead weight. That's all I wanted from the pack.

return-2.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: It is. I'll own that. People don't quit things loudly. They get bored, and then one day the bag's empty and they don't refill it.

return-3.speaker: LIQUID I.V.
text: Also fair. A routine's allowed to end. Four flavors shouldn't get a vote in that.
